transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-18 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood PM); Alex (Northstar CTO), Priya (ML Eng), Samir (Platform), Maya (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on prefetch/prefix and KV cache recommendations, routing policy options for cost vs latency, and an initial cost model for a pilot dedicated pool. Action items captured.

Topics: intro, traffic profile, prefix vs KV cache tradeoffs, prefetch heuristics, batching & concurrency knobs, cost model walkthrough, pilot next steps, security notes.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro - I'm Ava from Redwood inference, Diego our SE, Lina on product. How's the timing for folks?
[00:00:08] Alex: good, thanks, yeah tight day but excited. We mainly want to see the Optimize recommendations — we have weird spikes and cost keeps creeping up.
[00:00:15] Priya: and we have 3 main routes, search, short-chat, and long-form summarization, with very different seq lengths.
[00:00:22] Diego: perfect, that maps well to the playbook. we'll walk through prefix caching (we sometimes call it prefetch) and KV cache for continuing chats, and then show a cost model that ties those to per-token unit economics.
[00:00:34] Samir: one quick ask — we need to keep traffic inside our VPC during the pilot, is that doable?
[00:00:39] Ava: yes, private deployment / dedicated can be VPC-backed — we'll note that for the pilot. we'll also include our security and SOC2 docs.
[00:00:46] Lina: (interject) quick agenda: 1) look at your sample traffic, 2) prefix vs KV tradeoffs, 3) prefetch heuristics and eviction, 4) cost spreadsheet and pilot ask.
[00:00:55] Alex: sounds good.

[00:03:12] Diego: okay so first, high-level — prefix caching works best when you have repeated prefixes, e.g., standard prompts, system messages, or templated instructions. you get large token savings immediately on generation if hit rate is high. KV cache is for continuation across steps — it reduces decode cost by reusing key/value tensors for autoregressive decoding. they are complementary.
[00:03:40] Priya: clarification: the KV cache only helps within a single request or across sequential requests in a session?
[00:03:44] Diego: good q — KV cache is per model instance across requests if you wire up session affinity routing (or the runtime manages the session). for multi-tenant hosted, we provide automatic prefix cache at the API layer; for dedicated/private you can control eviction and affinity more tightly. sometimes transcription shows 'K-V cash' but it's KV cache.

[00:06:05] Ava: we pulled together a cost example for your traffic — rough numbers: baseline small-model hosted cost ~ $0.003/token for the model we benchmarked (note: placeholder), larger fine-tuned at $0.01/token. with prefix cache hit rates of ~40% on search routes we estimated 25-30% cost savings; with KV reuse on conversational flows you can get another 15% on decode costs.
[00:06:27] Maya: how are you modeling batching effects with tail latency? we've been burned by batching causing spikes in p99.
[00:06:34] Diego: great point — Optimize recommends dynamic batching thresholds and latency SLO-driven batch windows. basically smaller windows for p99-sensitive routes (chat) and aggressive batching for background batch jobs (summarization). the console exposes per-route batch window and target latency.
[00:07:01] Alex: are these batch windows per model or per route?
[00:07:04] Lina: per route, you can pin a model and batch config per route — so search can batch aggressively on the smaller model while chat uses low-latency config on a quantized variant.

[00:09:20] Priya: show us an example of prefetch heuristics — how do you decide to prefetch prefixes?
[00:09:25] Diego: we use a lightweight LRU + score-based prefetch: recent prefixes above a frequency threshold are prefetched into the runtime's prefix cache. heuristics include recency, frequency, and a cost saving estimate (expected tokens saved * model token cost). you can tune the frequency threshold in console, or let Optimize recommend a threshold based on historical hist.
[00:09:58] Priya: hist?
[00:10:00] Diego: traffic histogram, sorry, voice got cut — the tool analyzes per-route seq length distribution and top N prefixes.

[00:11:30] Samir: curious about eviction — if our cache is limited, do you evict by cost-savings or recency?
[00:11:34] Diego: typically cost-savings first (evict items with low benefit) then LRU as tie-breaker. for KV cache we often size based on active sessions; we also expose eviction windows so you can trade memory for hit rate.

[00:13:05] Ava: there's also routing policies — for cost control we can route by policy: e.g., route to smaller quantized model under normal load and fallback to full model on errors or for flagged users. you can set circuit-breaker thresholds and burst capacity.
[00:13:22] Alex: can we do region-based routing? our EU users need data residency.
[00:13:26] Lina: yes, region routing and residency tags are supported; for private deployments you can keep the whole control plane in your VPC.

[00:15:40] Diego: now i'll open the spreadsheet (link shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/sheets/optimize-northstar-pilot) — this is illustrative: columns = route, avg_seq_len, p95_seq_len, qps, prefix_hit_est, kv_reuse_est, per_token_cost, estimated_monthly_tokens, savings_est. the formula applies hit rate to saved input tokens and KV reuse to decode tokens.
[00:16:01] Priya: those default per-token numbers look higher than our current internal model cost — are these gross or net?
[00:16:05] Ava: they're gross model execution costs including infra overhead; for dedicated pools we show committed-rate discounts. we also model amortized GPU memory and kernel efficiency — e.g., A100 vs H100 differences.
[00:16:18] Samir: any gotchas on quantization affecting quality? we've seen subtle hallucination regressions at int8.
[00:16:24] Diego: yes, that's why Optimize includes quantization profiles per workload — we run a lightweight eval on your prompt set to detect quality regressions, and suggest mixed-precision or per-layer tunings rather than blanket int8. we'll ship the eval harness for you to run.

[00:18:42] Maya: okay walk me through an example: search route has avg_seq 30 tokens, p95 120, qps 80, we get a 35% prefix hit. what's the net saving?
[00:18:50] Diego: so quick math — with a 35% prefix hit, input tokens saved ~0.35 * avg_in_tokens per request. if model cost is $0.003/token and average total tokens per call is 60, then per-request cost drops by ~0.35*input_tokens*$0.003 — placeholder math in sheet shows ~22% cost reduction before batching improvements. plus with batching you multiply GPU throughput so amortized per-token infra cost decreases further.
[00:19:24] Priya: can Optimize simulate different batch sizes and show p99 impact?
[00:19:28] Lina: yes, simulation mode uses your histogram to model latency distribution under different batch windows; it outputs expected p50/p95/p99 and cost per million tokens. we'll run that for your routes in the pilot.

[00:22:10] Alex: on security — we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for model versions used. can you capture that?
[00:22:16] Ava: absolutely — private has KMS integration, per-model version audit logs, and RBAC. we'll include the compliance pack and SOC2 report.

[00:24:05] Samir: about the pilot sizing: we want to test under 2x peak traffic for a week. what's the recommended dedicated pool size?
[00:24:12] Diego: for a 2x peak test we recommend reserving capacity equal to estimated 1.5x peak QPS with auto-burst enabled; include a secondary fallback region or smaller model route. in the sheet we give suggestions per GPU type.

[00:26:40] Priya: latency SLOs — we want chat p99 < 350ms, search p99 < 200ms. can you meet that with batching and prefix?
[00:26:48] Diego: yes for chat we suggest low-latency model + small batch window and high session affinity so KV cache is effective; prefix cache reduces the generation length. search is easier — smaller model + aggressive batching. we often meet those SLOs in dedicated setups; we'll run bench to confirm.

[00:29:12] Alex: any limitations on prefix extraction? we have dynamic system messages that change a lot.
[00:29:18] Diego: if system messages are highly dynamic, prefix cache hit will be lower. Optimize helps by extracting stable sub-prefixes (like standard instruction blocks) and either normalizing variable fields or synthesizing templated tokens for caching. it's not magic but it often finds meaningful savings.

[00:31:30] Maya: what's the rollout plan? we want canary to 5% of traffic then ramp.
[00:31:34] Lina: console supports rollouts by route: you can do canary, A/B, or gradual ramp with automatic rollback on quality regressions. we also integrate with your Slack for alerts.

[00:33:55] Priya: are there any hidden costs in maintaining prefix cache (memory, compute)?
[00:34:00] Diego: main cost is memory and small CPU for cache management; we factor that into per-GPU utilization. Optimize's cost model includes amortized cache memory per active route. in many cases the savings far exceed the memory cost.

[00:36:10] Ava: quick demo of the console view (screen-share noted): per-route panel shows hit rate, top prefixes, estimated monthly savings, and recommended batch windows. you can toggle 'apply recommendations' to auto-provision settings to the runtime.
[00:36:35] Alex: will we be able to preview the changes before applying?
[00:36:40] Lina: yes simulation mode will show expected savings and latency shifts. we never force changes without your approval.

[00:38:50] Diego: small note on model variants: when capacity is constrained the router can fall back to a quantized variant or smaller architecture for non-SLO traffic. this reduces tail spikes across the pool.
[00:39:07] Priya: how do we validate quality post-rollout? can we tie regressions to prompt-level evals?
[00:39:12] Lina: yes we attach prompt sets and evals to rollouts; console flags regressions and can optionally block rollout if metric drift crosses thresholds.

[00:41:00] Alex: perfect. next steps then?
[00:41:04] Ava: we'll send the tailored spreadsheet and the playbook link: https://redwood.ai/docs/optimize-playbook, and you'll send the anonymized traffic histograms. we'll schedule the pilot kickoff — propose Tue 2025-07-29.
[00:41:20] Priya: works for us, we'll aim to upload logs by Monday.

[00:43:55] Samir: last thing — procurement wants an estimate for dedicated pricing. can you provide a committed discount band?
[00:44:02] Ava: yes we'll include committed rate examples in the follow-up. for a 6-12 month reserve we can show tiered discounts.

[00:46:10] Diego: one caveat — quantization + heavy batching can sometimes amplify certain failure modes; we'll put guardrails in the rollout.
[00:46:20] Maya: understood. thanks everyone.
[00:46:30] Ava: thanks all, recap in chat and action items — we'll follow-up with the spreadsheet and security pack.
[00:47:00] Alex: thanks, appreciate it.

[End of recording]
